Let \(y_i=\cos x_i\). Then \(y_i\in[-1,1]\), \(\sum y_i=0\), and
\[
\cos(3x_i)=4\cos^3x_i-3\cos x_i=4y_i^3-3y_i.
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{10}\cos(3x_i)
=4\sum_{i=1}^{10}y_i^3-3\sum_{i=1}^{10}y_i
=4\sum_{i=1}^{10}y_i^3.
\]
So we maximize \(\sum y_i^3\) subject to \(\sum y_i=0\), \(|y_i|\le1\).

At the maximum, the positive \(y_i\)'s are as large as possible, and the negative magnitudes are equal. Hence the optimal form is
\[
m\text{ entries equal to }1,\qquad
s\text{ entries equal to }-\frac{m}{s},
\]
with \(m\le s\) and \(m+s\le10\). Then
\[
\sum y_i^3=m-s\left(\frac{m}{s}\right)^3
=m-\frac{m^3}{s^2}.
\]
For fixed \(m\), this is maximized by taking \(s=10-m\). Checking \(1\le m\le5\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
m=1&:\quad 1-\frac1{81},\\
m=2&:\quad 2-\frac8{64}=\frac{15}{8},\\
m=3&:\quad 3-\frac{27}{49}=\frac{120}{49},\\
m=4&:\quad 4-\frac{64}{36}=\frac{20}{9},\\
m=5&:\quad 0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The maximum is \(\frac{120}{49}\), attained by three \(1\)'s and seven \(-\frac37\)'s. Therefore
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{10}\cos(3x_i)=4\cdot\frac{120}{49}
=\boxed{\frac{480}{49}}.
\]
